summary: The note describes a series of autumn folk music festivals returning after September 1, 2023: the Highland Harmony Festival, Bluegrass Bonanza, and Appalachian Anthems weekend. It covers heritage, international acts, transformed venues, intergenerational bonding, workshops, food, inclusivity, eco-friendly initiatives, and resilience, with quotes from organizers, performers and attendees.
one_line: Overview of autumn 2023 folk music festivals in Scotland, Kentucky and West Virginia, covering performances, workshops, food, inclusivity and sustainability.
key_facts: The Highland Harmony Festival takes place on September 12, in the hills of old Scottish grounds near the loch of Lomond.
The Bluegrass Bonanza takes place on October 5 against the backdrop of the Kentucky woodlands.
The Appalachian Anthems weekend takes place on November 3 in the rolling hills of West Virginia, with temporary stages and tents.
Fiona Campbell, organizer of the Highland Harmony Festival, says the festival is 'an invitation to travel back through time and relive the stories that have shaped our identity.'
Sunita Bhowmick, an Indian sitar virtuoso, performs at the Bluegrass Bonanza and is famed for fusing classical ragas with Appalachian reels.
Michael Hawkins, organizer of Appalachian Anthems, compares the event each year to 'birthing a small village dedicated to the celebration of Appalachian culture.'
Jane Thompson attended the Highland Harmony Festival with her grandson to share what she loved in her youth, saying 'It's about heritage.'
'Bowin' Bob Franks, a revered fiddler, hosts masterclasses at the Bluegrass Bonanza that become an instant hit.
Peter Monroe is a coordinator who says the festivals foster an environment of learning and appreciation of craftsmanship.
Food includes haggis and black pudding at Highland Harmony and smoky pit barbecue at Appalachian Anthems.
Chef Emilia Rodriguez curates a farm-to-table experience at the festivals.
The Tokyo Taiko Ensemble performs at the Bluegrass Bonanza; member Kenji Tanaka speaks of traditional beats moving a crowd thousands of miles from home.
Eco-friendly initiatives include recycling programs, zero-waste policies, and an emphasis on sustainability.
